newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower on tightening liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower on tightening liquidity.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower on Wednesday as recently soaring money rates and expectation of impending rate hikes by commercial banks continued to trap the market in caution, brokers said.
The weighted index fluttered in a tight range for most of the session before closing 58.21 points or 0.59 percent lower at 9,861.47.
Turnover was relatively moderate at T$169.55 billion.
Brokers said buying sentiment was dampened sharply after the 30-day commercial paper soared to 8.75 percent at mid-session on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.00 close.
The benchmark index has gained more than 40 percent in an extended bull run that covered most of 1997. But the market has been hit by profit-taking in the past few sessions.
"The tightening liquidity is trapping the market in caution, and there is not much price-chasing willingness right now," said David Yu, vice president of International Investment Trust.

Electronics, which had led the market during much of 1997, fell 1.79 percent. Financials dropped 0.86 percent on concerns over impending bank rate hikes following the central bank's raising of two interest rates on Thursday.
The only sector that saw substantial gains was constructions, which rose 2.58 percent. The sector had lagged behind others during the market's previous charge.
Brokers said they expected caution to last into Thursday.
